newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK SHARES FIRM IN SELECTIVE TRADE, OFF HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: TURK SHARES FIRM IN SELECTIVE TRADE, OFF HIGHS.

text.p: Istanbul shares ended higher in range-bound and selective trade on Wednesday, but fell from earlier highs on resistance and the possibility of early elections to be held this year, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed up 16 points, or 0.97 percent at 1,660 after dropping from a morning high of 1,671.
Daily trade volume increased to 22.73 trillion lira from yesterday's 14.78 trillion.

"The index still faces a major barrier at 1,700 although the outlook looks positive because the market is likely to continue its upward move with inner dynamics," said Serdar Surer from Ekinciler securities.
"If there is no negative news on the political front, I expect the index to test 1,750 at the highest although trade volume is still not so high," he added.
Brokers said the morning rise was a reaction to the sharp fall from Friday's trading high of 1,700 to Tuesday's intra-day low of 1,620 percent drop.
Remarks by members of the ruling coalition's Islamist and conservative parties prompted sales in the afternoon after which the index traded in a very tight band.
A senior member of the Islamist Welfare Party (RP) said elections were expected to take place in October to solve a growing row between the coalition and the secularist establishment.
"During this month the election decision will be made by parliament and elections will probably take place in October," RP deputy Temel Karamollaoglu told a news conference.
Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller also said there would be a change of government within days to solve the row.
"A change of government is expected in the coming days," Ciller told deputies from her True Path Party (DYP) in parliament.

Ciller and Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan announced on June 1 that they would seek early elections to overcome a growing dispute with the secular establishment over demands for a crackdown on religious activism.
A polling date has not yet been set, but it would have to be approved by parliament where the Islamist-conservative coalition has a thin majority.
Failure to pass a law to hold snap polls by the end of 1997 might give the secularist opposition the chance to form the new alliance which the stock market has been hoping for, brokers said.

Of the 245 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 114 to 60 and 71 were steady. The IMKB Industrial gained 1.31 pct to 1,547, IMKB Services went up 1.28 pct to 1,659 and IMKB Financial edged up 0.55 pct to 1,820.

Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 225,000, car maker Tofas Oto Fabrika, up 1,000 lira at 8,600 and largely state-owned oil refiner Tupras, down 1,000 lira at 80,000. They made up about 18 percent of the total turnover.
